restated: Let f(q,r) be defined by the Brouwer recurrence (MISSION section 2), B_c(x)=f(c+x,c)-(c+x) when f(c+x,c)>=c+x (undefined otherwise). For each row c let p_c be its eventual period (p_c=1 if row c has only finitely many P-positions [p,q,c] with p>=q) and N(c) its preperiod as in MISSION, with N(c) = 1 + the last such q for a row with finitely many. For r>=1 let q_r = lcm{p_c : c<r}, sigma_r = max_{c<r} N(c) - r (the index set c<r always contains c=0, so both are finite; at r=1, q_1=p_0 and sigma_1=N(0)-1), and V''(a) = union over c<r of {B_c(a+r-c)} (defined values only). Then a -> V''(a) is q_r-periodic for all a >= max(sigma_r,0). This lemma claims no bound on any N(c).
ledger_statement: DETERMINISM ONSET (structural; no bound claimed). For every r>=1, V''(a) is q_r-periodic for all a >= max(sigma_r,0), sigma_r := max_{c<r} N(c) - r, where for a stale row N(c) is 1 + the last q with a P-position [p,q,c], p>=q. Proof componentwise: V''_{r,c}(a)=B_c(a+r-c) is evaluated at x>=u_c=N(c)-c iff a>=N(c)-r, where B_c is p_c-periodic (live c) or undefined (stale c). Hence the merged-trail machine is autonomous from a=max(sigma_r,0). sigma_r is expressed through the N(c), c<r; the lemma does not bound them.
